subject: physics
title: Atmospheric pressure
key_idea: (Separate science) The atmosphere is a thin layer of air around the Earth. Air particles colliding with a surface create atmospheric pressure. Pressure decreases with height because there is less air above.

sections.heading: A simple model of the atmosphere

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what the atmosphere is and how it creates pressure.

items: The atmosphere is a layer of air around the Earth.
The layer is thin compared with the size of the Earth.
Air particles collide with every surface in the atmosphere.
The atmosphere is a thin layer of air around the Earth.
Atmospheric pressure is caused by air particles colliding with a surface.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section explains why atmospheric pressure is lower at greater height.

items.text: The height of the surface above the ground increases.
The number of air particles above the surface decreases, so the weight of air above it decreases.
Atmospheric pressure decreases as height increases.

diagram.alt: A sketch showing atmospheric pressure falling as height above the Earth's surface increases. It shows the shape only.

items: A walker climbing a hill has less air above them at the top, so the pressure is lower.
A balloon rising through the atmosphere meets a lower pressure outside it.
A skydiver falling towards the ground has more air above them, so the pressure on them increases.
As height increases there is less air above a surface.
So atmospheric pressure decreases with an increase in height.
Falling towards the ground, the weight of air above increases and so the pressure increases.

checks.q: Explain why atmospheric pressure decreases as a student climbs a mountain.
checks.a: There is less air above the student, so the mass of air above decreases. Fewer air particles are above them.

checks.q: A helium balloon rises through the atmosphere. Describe what happens to its size and explain why.
checks.a: It gets bigger. The pressure outside the balloon decreases because there are fewer air particles above, so the pressure inside is greater than outside.
Air particles colliding with a surface.

worked_example.question: In a world record attempt, a skydiver jumped from a height of 40 km above the Earth. Explain why the atmospheric pressure acting on the skydiver increased as the skydiver fell.
answer_points: There is a greater weight of air above the skydiver as the distance fallen increases.
Pressure = force ÷ area, so the pressure increases.
OR the density of the air around the skydiver increases as the skydiver falls.
OR there are more frequent collisions of air particles with the skydiver, so the pressure increases.
worked_example.tip: Give either the weight of air route or the density and collisions route. Two marks in total.

blocks.text: The atmosphere gets less dense with increasing altitude. The air is thinner higher up.

worked_example.question: A balloon is filled with helium when it is on the ground. The balloon is released and it rises through the atmosphere. Explain what happens to the size of the balloon as it rises through the atmosphere.
answer_points: As the balloon rises it gets bigger.
The density of air decreases, so there are fewer air particles in the atmosphere.
The pressure outside the balloon decreases.
The pressure inside the balloon is greater than the pressure outside.
worked_example.tip: One mark for 'gets bigger' and then any two reasons. The two reason marks can be earned even if the first is missed.

worked_example.question: Explain how and why atmospheric pressure changes with height above the surface of the Earth.
answer_points: There is less atmosphere (air) above, pushing down.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the change and one for the reason. 'Fewer particles above it' is allowed. Gravity and density are ignored.

extra.heading: The simple model of the atmosphere

items: The atmosphere is a single layer of gas that covers the Earth.
It covers the Earth to a height of about 700 km.
The density of the air is uniform.
Knowledge of layers is not expected.
